strategies.title: Blue-green
strategies.summary: Run v2 as a complete second environment, test it with no users, then switch all traffic at once.
pros: Instant rollback while blue still runs
Test the real environment before users see it
No mixed versions serving at once
cons: Double the infrastructure during the release
Shared databases must work with both versions
azure: App Service deployment slots: deploy to staging, warm up, swap
Front Door or Traffic Manager switching between two environments
AKS: two Deployments, switch the Service selector

strategies.title: Canary
strategies.summary: Send a small share of real traffic to v2, watch its metrics, and raise the share in stages.
cons: Two versions serve at once, so they must be compatible
Needs good monitoring to judge the canary
azure: Azure Pipelines Kubernetes manifest task with strategy: canary
App Service traffic routing: a percentage to a slot
Argo Rollouts or Flagger on AKS

strategies.title: Rolling
strategies.summary: Replace instances a few at a time; traffic moves as new instances become ready.
pros: No extra environment (only a small surge)
Built into Kubernetes and VM scale sets
cons: Probes say it is up, not that it is right
azure: AKS Deployment rollingUpdate (maxSurge, maxUnavailable); kubectl rollout undo
VM scale set rolling upgrade policy
Azure Pipelines strategy: rolling with maxParallel on VM environments

strategies.title: Ring-based
strategies.summary: Promote the release through rings of users - internal, early adopters, one region, everyone - with a bake time and health gate between them.
pros: Blast radius grows only when the previous ring is healthy
Matches how large services (and Azure itself) roll out
Automatic halt on a failed gate
cons: Slow: days or weeks to reach everyone
Needs ring targeting and per-ring health signals
azure: Azure Pipelines stages per ring with approvals and gates (e.g. query Azure Monitor alerts)
Feature flags in Azure App Configuration targeting rings

quiz.question: You need rollback in seconds, can pay for a second environment during the release, and run on App Service.
quiz.explanation: Deployment slots are blue-green: swap to release, swap back to roll back.

quiz.question: A new recommendation model should face 5% of real users, and you'll decide on its click-through and error metrics.
quiz.explanation: A canary exposes a small share of real traffic and is judged on metrics before the weight goes up.

quiz.question: A stateless API on AKS. You want zero downtime and no extra environment.
quiz.explanation: The default Deployment strategy: replace pods a few at a time behind readiness probes.

quiz.question: Dogfood internally first, then a preview audience, then region by region.
quiz.explanation: Ring-based: each ring is a bigger audience behind a health gate.

quiz.question: Rollback must not need a redeploy, but you can't afford two full environments.
quiz.explanation: Rolling back a canary is just weight 0% and removing one instance; v1 never stopped serving.

quiz.question: v2 passes readiness probes but returns wrong prices. Which strategy, watching only probes, would put it in front of everyone?
quiz.explanation: Rolling trusts readiness probes. Canary and ring gates look at business and error metrics before going wider.
